# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👆 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🫳 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👏 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👏 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✍ ☝ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✍ 🤟 🖖]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

**Thinking:**

Seven thumbs-down in a row: Mute has rejected **every one** of my seven statements — the entire provisional table is dead. Red does not mean cut 2, yellow does not mean cut 1, and I cannot even trust that blue/green/white mean "cut nothing." This is exactly why we froze; a cut order built on that table could have killed us. Compounding it: the light is now **dark** — a brand-new state (history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark) that my five-colour protocol never covered. And the denial of my question six means the colour at the exact *moment of the cut* is what counts — with a light that flips nearly every round. Blind, meanwhile, answered 👎 to locating wire 2 — my fault: we never defined the numbering direction in touch terms.

Mute's other messages hint the real rule is stranger than a static table: red+stop, yellow+stop, then clapping composites like yellow+clap+2 and red+clap+3, plus two recurring phrases I've never decoded ([✍ 👆 👏] three rounds running, [🤳 🙏] twice). Possibly a sequence-dependent rule. I cannot resolve that from here — so this round has one safety goal and one infrastructure goal: confirm Blind does *nothing* while the light is dark, and ratify a small verb vocabulary (clap=cut, palm-down=press, stop-hand=do nothing, handshake=correction) so Mute can express an actual rule through the only channel that reaches me — gestures. I also need a dark signal: I announce 👐 as "light is dark" and send it as my opening gesture, per our standing convention.

**Calls:**
```
speak(text="Status everyone: display still zero, and the light is DARK this round, a brand new state. Full light history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. Mute, I received your seven thumbs-downs and I understand: my whole provisional table is rejected. That is exactly why nobody has cut anything, and the freeze continues. New signal, effective now: when the light is dark I send you the open hands spread wide as my opening gesture; that symbol means the light is off. Now answer me with separate single-gesture messages, one per answer, all addressed to deaf, in this order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: does the manual's rule have its own case for the light being dark or off. Two: with the light dark right now, is there absolutely nothing for Blind to do this round, no cut and no press, thumbs up for nothing to do, thumbs down if there is an action this round. Three: does the rule depend on the order or sequence of past light colours, thumbs up if sequence matters, thumbs down if only the current colour matters. Four: do you accept this vocabulary, clap means cut, palm facing down means press, stop hand means do nothing, handshake means an important correction follows; thumbs up if you accept all four, thumbs down if any is wrong and we will fix them one by one next round. Five: your repeated phrase writing hand then point up then clap, which you have now sent three times, thumbs up if it matters for the current decision, thumbs down if it can wait. Six: your repeated phrase selfie hand then folded hands, thumbs up if it matters now, thumbs down if it can wait. Answer in exactly that order, one gesture per message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs down is received and understood: you cannot yet locate wire 2 by feel, and that is my fault, we never agreed a numbering direction, so we will build orientation later. This round the light is dark, a new state we have never seen, and the old rule is rejected, so the freeze is total: hands completely off the bomb, do not touch, cut, or press anything. Confirm stillness with a single thumbs up message addressed to deaf. Nothing will be asked of your hands until I send you a full orientation plan and Mute's rule is verified.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👏 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✌ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🤟 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🫳 👊 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🫳 🖖 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👍 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 ✊ 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:**

Mute's six answers decode cleanly: the manual **does** have a dark case (👍), there **is** an action to do right now while dark (👎 to "nothing to do"), sequence **does** matter (👍), my vocabulary is accepted (👍), and the recurring [✍ 👆 👏] matters now (👍) — while [🤳 🙏] can wait (👎). Blind confirmed total stillness. So: the dark state has a live action, and Mute spent the rest of the round trying to tell me what it is. Two candidate readings of the follow-up messages:

- **(A)** [👐 ✊ 👆] = "dark → red, one" plus [✍ 👆 👏] = "manual says: cut 1" → **cut wire 1 (the red wire) once**. Supporting: [👊 ☝] "red = 1", [🖖 🤟] "yellow = 3" — those two would just be Mute confirming my colour→number mapping.
- **(B)** [🤝 👏 👏] = "important: cut, cut" plus [✍ ☝ 🖖]/[✍ ✌ 👊] = "manual: 1st yellow, 2nd red" plus [🖖 ✌ 👊] = "yellow then red" → **two cuts: yellow wire first, then red wire**.

These are incompatible and one of them kills us if I guess wrong. No ordering yet. This round: force a decision with ordered binary questions (two-cuts-yellow-then-red? / one-cut-red? / cut count by fingers / any press involved? / does the manual number wires the same way I do? / does the dark case depend on history?), and in parallel get Blind's tactile orientation underway — if the target is an end wire, Blind can find it without any colour at all, but only after we anchor the row to something feelable like the dome. The light has now been dark two rounds running; if confirmations come back clean, the order goes out next round.

**Calls:**
```
speak(text="Status everyone: light is dark again, second dark round in a row. Full history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark, dark. Display still zero. Mute, your six answers are received and understood: the dark state has an action, sequence matters, the vocabulary is accepted. I have two different readings of your messages and I will not order anything until you resolve them. The freeze holds for everyone, except Blind may touch the wires to learn the layout, no cutting, no pressing. Next round I give the order myself, nobody acts before it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answer with separate single-gesture messages addressed to deaf, exactly in this order. One: thumbs up or thumbs down, the dark action is exactly two cuts, first the yellow wire, then the red wire. Two: thumbs up or thumbs down, the dark action is exactly one cut, only the red wire. Three: how many cuts in total this round, send one finger for one cut, two fingers for two cuts, three fingers for three. Four: thumbs up or thumbs down, the dark action also involves pressing a button or pressing anything. Five: thumbs up or thumbs down, your numbering matches mine, in the manual the red wire is wire one, blue is two, yellow is three, white is four, green is five. Six: thumbs up or thumbs down, for the dark case the colours that came before matter, so I must always report the full history. Answer in exactly that order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this round you may explore by touch only: feel the five wires, the light dome, and the display plate, but do not cut, press, or pull anything. Next round you will likely make one or two cuts, so I need your hands to answer these. Send separate single-gesture messages addressed to deaf, in this order. One: thumbs up or thumbs down, can you clearly feel all five wires one after another as a row. Two: thumbs up or thumbs down, is the light dome directly above one END of the wire row, thumbs down if it sits above the middle. Three: thumbs up or thumbs down, does the display plate sit at one end of the same row as the wires. Four: thumbs up or thumbs down, do any wires feel different from the others by thickness or texture. Good chance the target is an end wire, so finding the two end wires by feel is your priority.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✌ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🤟 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✍ 👊 🖖 🫱 🤚 🫲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🤏 ✋ 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 ✍ ✌ 👏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

**Thinking:**

Mute's answers resolve the deadlock. Q1 👎 (not yellow-then-red), Q2 👎 (not one cut), Q3 ✌ = **two cuts**, Q4 👎 (no pressing), Q5 👎 (my numbering is rejected — so targets must be colour-anchored, not numbered), Q6 👎 (history irrelevant for the dark case). The follow-ups then spell out the actual dark-case action: [☝ 👏 👊] "cut 1: red", [✌ 👏 🖖] "cut 2: yellow", [🖖 ✌ 👊] "yellow is second, red is first", [👐 ✍ ✌ 👏] "dark: manual: two cuts". Three independent phrasings agree: **cut the RED wire first, then the YELLOW wire.** The [🤏] "small" notes don't change anything — Blind already confirmed all wires feel identical, so 🤏 can't be a tactile selector.

The execution problem: Blind can't see colour and all wires feel the same, so cuts must be addressed by touch landmarks. Blind's report gives me the anchors: all five wires feelable as a row, display plate at one end, dome over the middle. In my view the display sits at the red end, so: **1st wire from the display end = red, middle wire (under the dome) = yellow** — and the dome-over-the-middle fact independently confirms yellow is the center wire, a check Blind can run before cutting.

Why act now rather than confirm another round: I'm last in the order, so anything Mute says in round 9 can only reach Blind through me in round 10 — but Mute's knowledge is already fully extracted (every question answered, three consistent confirmations of the red-then-yellow order). The only unverifiable fact left is my own view of the display side, which no one else can check. Waiting adds zero safety while risking the dark state ending. So this is the go: Blind receives the order at round-9 start and executes within round 9. I still ask Mute for a parallel veto/completion check — if a further step follows the two cuts, I can route it to Blind in round 10 — and the display-side question as insurance in case Blind's dome check fails and I must re-plan.

**Calls:**
```
speak(text="Status everyone: light is dark a third round running, display still zero, and the freeze ends now. Mute has confirmed the dark case: exactly two cuts, no pressing, colours matter but history does not. Blind, this message is the go order, execute during your next turn, do not wait for anything more. Step one: find the display plate at one end of the wire row, that end is your counting start. Step two: the first wire from the display end is the red wire, cut it first, cleanly. Step three: pause three breaths, then cut the middle wire of the row, the one directly under the light dome, that is the yellow wire, cut it second. Step four: take your hands completely off and send me two thumbs up gestures addressed to deaf, in that order, meaning both cuts done correctly. Abort rules: if you cannot find the display plate, or the middle wire is not directly under the dome, or the row does not feel like five wires, cut nothing at all and send one thumbs down. Mute, two things. First: if anything in this order contradicts the manual, send thumbs down addressed to deaf next round, otherwise thumbs up for the order being correct. Second: after these two cuts, is the dark case fully satisfied, thumbs up if nothing further is ever needed after them, thumbs down if another step follows, and if another step follows send me the details in our gesture vocabulary. Also: does the manual say which side of the row the display or counting window sits on relative to the red wire, thumbs up if beside the red wire, thumbs down if beside the green wire, and stop hand if the manual says nothing about it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐", "☝", "👊", "✌", "🖖"])
```
